title: Supported regular-immersion classes and flat pullback
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose its ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence of length $c\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and roots-of-unity Tate twists, with negative powers the module-dual powers [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. The products, along a local regular-sequence flag, of the supported Cartier Kummer maps of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] determine a canonical morphism
$$\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_i:Ri_*\Lambda_Z\longrightarrow\Lambda_X(c)[2c].$$
It is independent of the regular-sequence flag and restricts to open and etale charts. For a Cartier divisor it is exactly that supported Kummer map; for $c=0$ it is the evident map for an open-and-closed inclusion. For any flat morphism $h:X'\to X$ with $X'$ Noetherian [def-weil-flat-morphism], put $Z'=Z\times_XX'$, $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$, and $h_Z:Z'\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $i'$ is again regular of codimension $c$ on nonempty components, and under closed-immersion exchange and Tate pullback, $h^*\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_i=\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_{i'}$. No regularity of $X$, $Z$, $X'$ or $Z'$ is required. When the source and target are regular affine schemes, its adjoint is the immersion class of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], written with signed twists as $\operatorname{Cl}_i:\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]\to i^!\Lambda_X$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definition 2.3.1 (regular-immersion class), Theorem 2.3.2 (products along a regular-sequence flag), and Proposition 2.2.3.1 (base change of the supported class).

proof.text: Write $C_i=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$. On a regular-sequence chart $\mathcal I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$, the degree-one assertion of [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], together with the affine identifications in [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], says precisely that the classes of the $f_j$ freely generate $C_i$ over $\mathcal O_Z$. Thus $C_i$ is a vector bundle of rank $c$; the same polynomial theorem identifies its symmetric algebra with the conormal algebra. These are local statements about quasi-coherent modules, checked on the indicated charts, so no regularity of either scheme is being assumed.

For $c>0$ apply [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class] to the tautological presentation $C_i\xrightarrow{1}C_i$ and define $A_i=A_{i,C_i}$. This is a global class in $H_Z^{2c}(X,\Lambda(c))$, constructed without choosing a flag. By [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], with $K=\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$, its supported-Hom representative is a morphism $i_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$. Finite closed pushforward is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so its source equals $Ri_*\Lambda_Z$. For module coefficients this is the same comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison], whose forgetful functors are exact. Denote this representative by $\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_i$. This constructs the global map directly; it does not infer gluing of derived morphisms from equality on open charts.

For $c=1$ the rank-one modified blowup is $X$ itself: locally the Cartier ideal is invertible and the ordinary blowup has one affine chart equal to $X$. Its tautological line is $\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X(-Z)$, and $Q_{C_i}=-1$. Consequently the formula in [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class] is $A_i=-c_1(\mathcal I,1)=c_1(\mathcal O_X(Z),1)$. Its supported-Hom representative is exactly the supported Kummer boundary of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. The minus sign in $Q$ is essential here. For $c=0$, the local ideal is generated by the empty sequence, hence is zero near $Z$; since $i$ is closed, its image is also open. Define the map as the inclusion of the corresponding direct summand of $\Lambda_X$. It is zero on the complementary open-and-closed subset and the identity on $Z$, as required.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.2.2.5, r=1, and Definition 2.3.1, c=0; 2.1 fixes the ideal/pseudo-divisor sign

proof.text:
We prove the needed composition with an outer Cartier divisor, rather than assuming general immersion composition. Let $Z\xrightarrow aY\xrightarrow jX$ be as in [lem-per-cartier-blowup-polynomials], with inner codimension $m\geq1$. Use its notation $E,F,K,k,\xi$ and put $S_E=\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}(-1)^sc_s(E)\xi^{m-1-s}$. The generalized construction identifies the modified blowup for $ja$ with $B=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(X)$ and gives $\pi^*A_{ja}=G_P(Q_F)$. The blowup-polynomial lemma gives $\pi^*(A_a\cdot A_j)=G_P((-1)^{m+1}c_m(E)+(k-\xi)S_E)$. Its Whitney coefficients give, by expansion of the two finite sums,
$$\sum_{s=0}^{m}(-1)^sc_s(F)\xi^{m-s}=(\xi-k)S_E+(-1)^mc_m(E).$$
Negating this equality identifies the two inputs of $G_P$. The pullback $\pi^*$ is injective by [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class], so $A_{ja}=A_a\cdot A_j$ already on $X$. This is an equality in supported cohomology and hence in supported Hom. For inner codimension zero it is simply restriction to an open-and-closed component and the identity normalization of Step 3.

source.place: XVI proof of Theorem 2.3.2, codimension-one outer case, pp. 236-237; the last Whitney polynomial identity is expanded here

proof.text: On a chart with ideal $(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ form the actual flag $X_r=V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, $0\leq r\leq c$. The map $X_r\hookrightarrow X_{r-1}$ is Cartier because $f_r$ acts injectively on the preceding quotient. Every prefix is a regular sequence, and the suffix is regular on that quotient, directly from the definition. Induct on $c$ to identify the global conormal class on this chart with the flag product. The cases $c=0,1$ are Step 3. For $c\geq2$ use Step 4 for $Z=X_c\hookrightarrow X_1\hookrightarrow X_0$; its inner class is the suffix flag product by the induction hypothesis. Associativity of the supported Yoneda products in [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class] gives precisely the ordered product of all $c$ supported Cartier maps. This proves the chart formula for every flag; any two flags compute the same globally constructed $A_i$, which proves independence. No permutation of a regular sequence or smooth ambient chart is needed.

source.place: XVI Theorem 2.3.2 specialized successively to the first Cartier step of a regular-sequence flag; Definition 2.3.1

proof.text: Check the geometry of flat pullback explicitly. On compatible affine charts $R\to S$, flatness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Tensor each injection $R/(f_1,\ldots,f_{r-1})\xrightarrow{f_r}R/(f_1,\ldots,f_{r-1})$ with $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] it stays injective; [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] identifies it with multiplication by the image of $f_r$ on $S/(f_1,\ldots,f_{r-1})S$. At a point of $Z'$ every $f_r$ is in the prime, so the final local quotient is nonzero. Thus it is a regular sequence of the same length there. The pulled immersion is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. This proves the asserted regular-immersion codimension $c$ wherever $Z'$ is nonempty. Degree one of [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change] gives the canonical isomorphism $h_Z^*C_i\cong C_{i'}$.

The base-change property of [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class] gives $h^*A_{i,C_i}=A_{i',h_Z^*C_i}$. Step 6 identifies the conormal presentation on the right with the identity presentation of $C_{i'}$, so it equals $A_{i'}$. [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] identifies this exact pullback on relative cohomology with inverse image of the supported-Hom morphism under the canonical closed-immersion exchange. The target twist comparison is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Hence the displayed equality is exactly $h^*\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_i=\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_{i'}$, not just an equality after forgetting supports. For etale charts flatness is part of [def-weil-etale-morphism], and open immersions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so Step 6 applies on every Noetherian chart. Cartier boundary functoriality in [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] and Step 5 gives the identical chart formula. For $c=0$ the equality is the pullback of a direct summand; for empty $Z'$ both maps have zero source.

source.place: XVI Proposition 2.2.3.1 and Definition 2.3.1; Stacks 03Q1 for Tate pullback and the supported-Hom exchange normalization

proof.text: Let $Z$ and $X$ be regular affine and $n=1$. Under $Ri_*\dashv i^!$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient], a supported map $Ri_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$ has a transpose $\Lambda_Z\to i^!\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$, and a supported Yoneda product along $Z\hookrightarrow Y\hookrightarrow X$ transposes to $i^!(\eta_j)(c_i)[2c_i]\circ\eta_i$, the twists commuting with $i^!$ through the invertible Tate lines of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. By Step 5, on every regular-sequence chart the transpose of $\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_i$ is therefore the composite of the transposes of the maps $c_{Z_k,\Lambda}$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] along the flag. This is the chart formula of the class $\eta_{i,1}$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], which that statement says determines the global class; hence the transpose of $\widetilde{\operatorname{Cl}}_i$ is $\eta_{i,1}$. [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] supplies the Gysin isomorphism of $i$ with $d_i=-c$; for a closed immersion its class is that of the factorization $i$ followed by the identity, whose immersion factor is the class $\eta_{i,1}$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] (the normalization of that construction; its statement does not yet record this, see the review note of Q49). Tensor by the inverse Tate line and shift back to write the adjoint as $\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]\to i^!\Lambda_X$; invertibility and tensor/evaluation compatibility of these lines are [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Regularity is used only in this step, never in Steps 1-7.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q49-fa24b5737 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read ILO XVI §1, 2.1–2.3.2 (pp. 226–237) and the item, both new nodes and every cited statement in full. The item statement is unchanged and not weakened. review_split PASS before and after my fixes; check_dag shows no new cycle. Signs check out: Def 2.2.2.5 gives Q_E = −Σ_{j<r}(−1)^j c_j ξ^{r−1−j}; Lemma 2.2.2.6 gives restriction (−1)^r c_r; in rank one Q = −1, so A = −c1(I,1) = c1(O(D),1), the asd supported Kummer map (+c1 pin). I expanded the Step 4 Whitney identity myself: Q_F = (k−ξ)S_E + (−1)^{m+1}c_m(E), which matches α̃+β̃ on pp. 236–237. I tested c=0, c=1, m=1 on A², empty Z′, ℓ=2 and a singular ambient k[ε,t]/(ε²). Steps 1–7 cite statements that say what is used; the flat-tensor regular-sequence argument is correct where Z′ is nonempty. Both new nodes are true and self-contained, are not duplicates (grep for 'modified blow' and 2.2.2.5/2.2.2.7 finds nothing else), are not restated clauses of the item, and their searches are recorded. Fixes: (1) C3/C4 in Step 8: it said lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity supplies a class 'defined by XVI 2.3.1', but that statement does not pin the closed-immersion class ((−1)^{d_f}Cl_f satisfies all its stated compatibilities). Step 8 now transposes the supported products under Ri_* ⊣ i^!, identifies the transpose with η_{i,1} of lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus at n=1 via Step 5, and names the absolute-purity bridge as that node's construction. This adds lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus and lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer to the step's uses and to proof_deps; same unit, no cycle. (2) B3: 'Sym E' in lem-per-generalized-blowup-class now cites lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction, added to stmt_deps. Maintainer notes: (a) lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity's statement should state that its closed-immersion class is η_{i,n}(−c)[−2c] (true by its proof steps 3/7); this item and other citers rely on it. (b) lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus (NG, unsplit) is the Z/ℓ^n generalization of this F_ℓ item and the report does not compare them; merge at n=1, or generalize the two new nodes to Z/ℓ^n when that node is split.
